quest.title: Deluge of Wrathful Waters
quest.description: This is the day you get out of prison, and you proceed to complete the paperwork for your release as arranged.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x875, Mora x38100, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x7

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Some time has passed since the incident in the Fortress of Meropide, and your sentence here is almost finished.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ahh... Now for a little rest after breakfast... This is the life~

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait a sec, isn't something important supposed to happen today...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh! Today's our big day! We're supposed to leave the Fortress of Meropide! C'mon, we've gotta go complete the release procedures now.

dialogues.speaker: Monglane
dialogues.text: Please sign here. This document will be effective immediately upon signing and you two may exit the Fortress of Meropide via the regular channels.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's been so long since we've been to the surface, let's hurry up and—

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh!?

dialogues.speaker: Monglane
dialogues.text: Ah? What's happening...?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Are you okay?

dialogues.speaker: Monglane
dialogues.text: I'm fine, thanks... But I wonder what that tremor was just now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's go ask the Duke.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Your Grace~!

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Ah, good to see you two. Is there something you wish to see me about?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah! What was with that earthquake just now?

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Ah, that. The tremor didn't originate from the seafloor... in fact, it seems it came from the surface.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Over the years of serving as the warden here, I've developed a sense for distinguishing between what occurs on the surface and what occurs underwater. Besides, the seal that Monsieur Neuvillette set in place won't fail so easily.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So the Fortress is okay?

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: If you recall our last incident, if there really were a problem, there would be crowds of inmates in a panic right now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh. You've got a point... Okay, seems we need to get back up to the surface and ask about what happened.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: By the way, do you know what day it is today?

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: I believe today is this month's pipe-cleaning day.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, seriously!?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Actually, today is the day we say goodbye to the Fortress.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Ah, yes. Have you completed your release papers?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yep!

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Ah, it's you two! Are you leaving now?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's right! Today is our last day in prison... But now that Paimon says that, it doesn't feel like we were confined here. It's actually been pretty nice.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: A lot of people have helped us out.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, yeah. Paimon feels fond of this place now.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Then be sure to come back and visit! I'll miss you.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: If you've signed the release papers, then you're free to go. The guards will escort you out.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're not going to see us off?

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Heh, I knew you would ask... Alright, sure. Let's go.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, you actually agreed... No worries, you must be busy. Paimon was just joking...

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Ah, so you do have a polite side, I see.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: After being down here for so long, I imagine you must feel like you're lacking companionship... Shall I come along too?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: No, that's alright. It's not like we'll never visit again.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, don't worry, we'll come back to see you! Paimon really likes the cafeteria here — the chefs sure do know how to make good grub.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: I hope you won't be here as convicts the next time I see you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We'll do our best to stay out of trouble!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, it seems our work in the Fortress of Meropide is finished. That's the end of another chapter in our journey. And since Neuvillette was the one who asked us to come here...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We should probably go report to him now. Next stop, the Palais Mermonia!

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: You're going to go see Monsieur Neuvillette? Haha, please pass on our kind regards.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: I'm sure just your regards will do, no?

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: I believe it would be the polite thing to do.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: You're right... I've heard the Palais has been terribly busy these days. Tell him that I hope he hasn't been overwhelmed by the recent string of troubles.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The Palais Mermonia sure is buzzing with activity today...

dialogues.speaker: Sedene
dialogues.text: Halt! Huh? Oh, it's you two! Apologies, Monsieur Neuvillette did say that you'd be welcome at any time...

dialogues.speaker: Isadora
dialogues.text: Excuse me, would you mind helping me take a look at this report?

dialogues.speaker: Sedene
dialogues.text: I'll be right there. Sorry, I've got my hands full here... You can see yourselves in.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Everyone's so busy. Seems a lot has been happening...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Neuvillette~!

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Hello. You've come at the right time, but you'll have to wait for just a moment, as there are some urgent matters I must tend to first.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: In the meantime, please, have a seat. If you'd like to have something to drink, let the Melusine outside know.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's alright, we just ate.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Very well, then.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's take a break over there while we wait for him to finish his work.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Alright, that should wrap things up for now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are you done with your work?

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Yes, sorry to keep you waiting.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Today should be the day you were released from the Fortress of Meropide, and it appears that you've managed to complete all the release paperwork.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's right, and we came here to see you right away.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You and Paimon tell Neuvillette everything that happened since the Primordial Sea incident, as well as your dream regarding Childe...

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Hmm, a massive whale...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Do you have any idea what that might be?

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Judging from your description, that cannot have occurred in any ordinary waters, but rather, something like the Primordial Sea.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: A whale of that size and shape cannot usually be found in the waters of Teyvat. Therefore... We can only assume that Childe is presently immersed in Primordial Seawater.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Immersed in Primordial Seawater? But how? ...And is he okay?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: He's not from Fontaine, so he won't dissolve.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, true... But how did he end up in the Primordial Sea? Can people even get there?

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Most people wouldn't be capable of entering in the first place. I'm not completely sure how he could have gotten there, myself.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: There's something we'd like to ask you about.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Yes, what is it?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What was that tremor we felt earlier?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah right, Paimon felt it too!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We asked the Duke, and he said it wasn't from underwater, so we figured you might know something about it.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: It turns out that I have just received a report about this particular matter. In fact, that's exactly what I was busy with a moment ago.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: The source of the tremor was here on the surface, near Poisson. After the shaking stopped, the water levels in the Poisson area rose at an alarming rate.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The water levels rose? Oh no — what about all the people there?

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Fortunately, the water levels only rose for a short period of time, and have already returned to normal now. However, I still have a bad feeling about the whole phenomenon...

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: If the change in water levels is connected with the leaking Primordial Seawater, then the situation in Poisson may be much worse than it appears.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Navia should be in Poisson, right? We need to go check on her!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yes, Spina di Rosula's headquarters is there.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: I would also like to go there as soon as possible, but I'm afraid I can't leave just yet. We must immediately formulate disaster prevention plans for the surrounding coastal areas to avoid potential catastrophes.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: I'll have to ask you two to go to Poisson first. I'll meet you there to check on the situation once I've finished things here.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sounds like a plan.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There's no time to lose — let's get going!

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Please be careful.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh no... What happened here...?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (All the buildings here seem to be in pretty rough shape now...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (There's nobody around... Were they all dissolved? No, let's not assume the worst yet...)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Navia should be around here, right? We need to make sure she's still... Uh, Paimon means, we need to check on her!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We haven't seen a single soul all the way here... Ohh, this is getting scary!

dialogues.speaker: Disaster Victim (M)
dialogues.text: Ah! What will I ever do now!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Look, there's someone on the roof over there!

dialogues.speaker: Spina di Rosula Member
dialogues.text: Just stay put, we're coming up. Watch your balance!

dialogues.speaker: Disaster Victim (M)
dialogues.text: Ah, alright... Just hurry!

dialogues.speaker: Desyree's Father
dialogues.text: *sigh* I'm not young anymore... How will I survive on my own?

dialogues.speaker: Desyree's Father
dialogues.text: *sobbing* Oh, my Desyree...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *sigh* He looks pretty sad.

dialogues.speaker: Disaster Victim (F)
dialogues.text: My leg... Ah, my leg...

dialogues.speaker: Disaster Victim (F)
dialogues.text: How could this have happened... Ah, it hurts...

dialogues.speaker: Spina di Rosula Member
dialogues.text: Just hang in there! Help is on the way! You can hold my hand if it makes you feel better.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, it's Navia! She's over there!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! Navia! Are you okay?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: You're here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We heard there was a situation in Poisson, so we came as quickly as we could.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Yes... As you can see, the water levels suddenly rose — it caused quite the disturbance, in fact.

dialogues.speaker: Spina di Rosula Member
dialogues.text: Demoiselle! There was a wounded resident next to a building southeast of here. We've already transported him to safety, but we've run out of medical supplies.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: He's wounded? How badly?

dialogues.speaker: Spina di Rosula Member
dialogues.text: He fell, so it's probably a broken leg. He's pretty shaken up. When the water level rose, he desperately climbed up to the roof. Once the water receded and he saw the ground, he became terrified and eventually...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: He jumped down, then.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Find the leader of Squad One and tell him to take the wounded resident to see a doctor. He should know where to go.

dialogues.speaker: Spina di Rosula Member
dialogues.text: Understood! I'll take over his search and rescue mission in the meantime!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Alright, you'll be in charge.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: I'm sorry, where were we...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, the situation in Poisson...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Ah, right. Allow me to explain.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: A little earlier, we suddenly heard a loud noise. At first, everyone thought that something might have exploded on the aquabus, but before we knew it, water started pouring out from everywhere.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: The rushing water seemed a little odd, almost like the unique color of Primordial Seawater. Some people didn't realize the danger and thought it was just ordinary water leaking from somewhere.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Everyone on the street who happened to be close to the water didn't have a chance to escape. As the water levels rose, they suddenly disappeared. They were all dissolved...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Those who realized what was happening started to flee in a panic, desperately trying to get to higher ground. Many were injured in the stampede, and some... some people fell from significant heights...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: The Spina di Rosula initiated rescue operations as quickly as possible, but there have been a lot of casualties. Fortunately, the water began to recede after some time, and the chaos came to an end.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: The water that flooded the area contained Primordial Seawater, so the lower levels of Poisson are still hazardous. To ensure everyone's safety, I've asked the people there to leave as soon as possible.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: No one knows if this could happen again. All we can do for now is try our best to help evacuate the residents. We still haven't completed the headcount, but we'll have some numbers soon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How awful... And all of this just came out of nowhere...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: ...It was quite frightening indeed. I only wish that everything that just happened was a bad dream.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is there any way we can help, Navia?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Thank you for being so willing to help in a moment of crisis like this. You don't know how much it means to me... I really... can't express how grateful I am.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Wait, we're missing some people, aren't we...?)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Don't say that, Navia. That's what friends are for...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: By the way, where are Melus and Silver?

response.speaker: Spina di Rosula Member
response.text: Demoiselle! We've got a situation here!

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Ah, I'll be right there!

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Sorry, I need to go for now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And off she goes... Seems it might be a while before she can take a break.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Navia walks around talking with many people and organizing various matters. Her decisions are clear and reasonable, her face is marred by a somber expression throughout...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: ...Okay, the wounded are being tended to, and we've finished a preliminary headcount. More support has just arrived, so I suppose I finally have a moment to focus on my own matters.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Of course, we should remain ready for anything and continue doing our best to rescue others. I'll be sure to have everyone at the Spina di Rosula ready to render assistance.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, would you two accompany me to my father's grave for a moment?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Right now?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...I understand.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Thank you.

choices.text: You can put us to work.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: ...Not a lot of people here, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, given the time of day and the whole situation in Poisson, Paimon doesn't think there'd be a ton of people here visiting graves...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Right. That's how things are now... The living are so exhausted that they've no strength to spare any words for the dead.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um, Navia...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: There's no need to push yourself so hard.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: *sobbing* ...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Navia!? What's wrong...?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Sorry, I... I just...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Melus and Silver... They won't ever come back here again...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: What should I do, Papa?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? What happened to them!?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Everyone agreed on the rescue plan, but still... I was the one who initiated it.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: They were helping evacuate the residents... but they couldn't leave in time...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: And they were caught in the seawater... *sobs*

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wh—What should we do?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: I've known them for so long... And I know they weren't afraid... But... But...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: I could at least hold a funeral for my father, and I know where he rests. But as for Melus and Silver, they're just gone... I just can't...

response.speaker: Melus
response.text: Everything looks so clean after it rains — even the gravestones. I didn't expect that you'd enjoy a glass of red wine in front of Master Callas's grave.

response.speaker: Silver
response.text: I can understand. Besides, the scenery here isn't half bad.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: See? It's not just me. I always want to bring something when I visit Papa. Perhaps we might even have a picnic. He wouldn't be angry, would he?

response.speaker: Melus
response.text: Ah! How could Master ever be upset with you, Demoiselle?

response.speaker: Melus
response.text: Yet the cemetery is the home of those who have passed, is it not? Everyone ends up here sooner or later, no matter who you are.

response.speaker: Silver
response.text: Buying yourself a plot in advance, are you?

response.speaker: Melus
response.text: Haha, no need yet. But when I do, I hope you'll let me be buried beside Master Callas, Demoiselle.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Hey, stop joking around!

response.speaker: Melus
response.text: Oh, I'm quite serious. That way, I'll save us both the trip to see each other whenever you visit your father's grave.

response.speaker: Silver
response.text: That makes sense. In that case, could I be buried on his other side?

response.speaker: Melus
response.text: After all, besides you, Demoiselle, the two of us could certainly be considered Master's closest companions, no?

response.speaker: Silver
response.text: Personally, I believe we fill those shoes just fine.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Haha, why are you bringing this up all of a sudden? Seriously... Alright, alright, I'll remember your requests.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: But I'd really prefer not to talk about this stuff. And what do you mean by "saving me a trip"!? I'd make the journey even if I had to visit you two somewhere else.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: I had promised to let them rest in peace here... but here I am, breaking that promise.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: I'm sorry for letting you see me in a mess like this... I don't usually cry, really.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon doesn't know how to help you feel better, but well, she understands how you feel...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: I had always thought I could make my wishes come true. But now that I think about it, that never solely relied on me. Many things can only be accomplished with someone else's help.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Melus and Silver have helped me so much, but by contrast, I could do nothing for them.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: ...I'm so sorry.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You can spend as much time as you need here, Navia. We'll stay with you.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Yeah, we're here for you.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Thank you. Right now... You don't know how much that means.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: By the way, you can have a look at this. It's a list of victims from the incident that took place here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Aubenas, Cannes, Bernette, Giverny... Francine, Korina... Desyree, Joinville... Jolienne, Essonnes... as well as Melus and Silver.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So... everyone else is safe? But still...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: It's okay, I know what you're thinking. And you're right — we lost Melus and Silver, but we were able to save more than we anticipated.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: ...The overall outcome indicates that the cost was worth it.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: No one's sacrifice is truly necessary.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right! Don't think that way, Navia. One person might be saved at the expense of another, sure, but that isn't something we should ever consider a "trade."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Melus and Silver were not the "price" for saving anyone. They're heroes!

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: You're right... Thank you, Paimon.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: What you said just now was pretty amazing, actually. I'll remember your words.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh? Uh, really?
Seems you've become more eloquent in the time since we last met.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... The Knave? What are you doing here?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Ah, is everything going well on your side?

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Yes. My people are carrying out the mission according to your request. All the residents of Poisson have been evacuated, and we are preparing to relocate them to higher ground.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: As for the supplies, we have everything taken care of... There is no need to worry.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Thank you very much.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, do you two know each other?

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: We just met recently. Right, Miss Navia?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Hmm... Usually, I would call this a coincidental encounter, but that doesn't quite fit this time... Besides, it never even crossed my mind that a Fatui Harbinger would come looking for me.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Thanks to The Knave, Spina di Rosula received generous support from the Fatui, which allowed us to complete the rescue and evacuation work so quickly.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Mutual aid is essential to fostering positive developments. We were already in the area, in any case, so it was nothing.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: That said, I must say that you're a lot sharper than you let on. I'm sure you understand what I mean.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: I apologize for all the ways in which I tested you previously. We've never worked with the Fatui before, and it's extremely important for us to know who we're working with.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: My subordinates have reported that Fatui soldiers have been observing water levels and taking headcounts in various locations. I hear that they've also prepared a large amount of emergency supplies... I'm quite surprised.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: This is nothing to brag about, nor do I intend to. It is simply the way of powerful organizations to act forcefully, whether they are doing good or ill — you've witnessed that firsthand, in any case.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: #As I've told {NICKNAME} before, I know of the prophecy, and I intend to prevent the impending disaster.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Lending your organization a hand was a natural first step in accomplishing that. As such, do not be troubled by this token of our sincerity. Perhaps, one day, you'll also be able to help me in the same way.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Without your help, there would have been many more casualties... I won't forget your kindness.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Furthermore, I sincerely regret what happened to Melus and Silver. I only wish that my people could have arrived a little earlier to prevent this from happening.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Don't say that... You and your subordinates did everything you could.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: As Paimon said, Melus and Silver didn't choose to sacrifice themselves for any specific person, and they weren't the "price" paid for others' salvation. They... chose to become heroes themselves.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: I've never liked hearing people put it that way. It's like trying to relieve pain by saying some noble-sounding words. But right now, there's nothing more suitable... they really did become heroes.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: You're right. I'm sorry for your loss, Miss Navia.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Water is life to Fontaine's people, and it also spells disaster. It's no wonder that people always say that prophecies represent fate. Fortunately, I've never been one for such opinions.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: So you're one who will try to change fate, then?

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Of course. That is why I'm going to Hotel Bouffes d'ete. I still have some things to take care of, and the children need my attention.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: #By the way, {NICKNAME}, Paimon. One more thing...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright, then we'll just... Uhh... Huh? This isn't right... Paimon thought you would ask us to walk with you for a moment so you could tell us something in private!

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: That is a clever and useful conversation technique, which I do like to use when necessary. But there's no need today — it would not hurt to have Miss Navia listening in.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, I'm sure you remember that I said we could work together when we had the chance.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: You and I both know that there may be issues with the Primordial Sea. Previously, it was the Fortress of Meropide's sluice gate, and this time, it was the water levels in Poisson... These are both signals.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So, the time for jolly cooperation has come?

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Indeed. Allow me to share the latest intel I've received from the House of the Hearth's intelligence network with you.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: During some recent investigations, a child claimed to have discovered some ruins near Poisson. The ruins date back to ancient times, and seem to be worth investigating in many ways.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Judging by the dating of the ruins, they may be related to the prophecy and the coming crisis. The situation is becoming more urgent, so any pertinent information will prove extremely precious.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: My people initially came to prepare for ruin exploration. Unexpectedly, this disaster struck... And at present, we're all busy prioritizing the rescue effort.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: So that's why the Fatui were all already in Poisson...

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: I wanted to take the children along, but unfortunately, Lyney, Lynette, and Freminet have all been dispatched to higher ground to assist affected residents.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Lyney told me that outside of the House, the person they trust most is you.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Which is why I want to give you this task.

choices.text: Are you sure this'll be okay?

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: The House of the Hearth's members see each other as family. But Lyney, Lynette, and Freminet said that they also see you as such, even though you are not from the House.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: I'm sure you already understand how earnest they consider their friendship with you to be.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, that somehow makes Paimon feel kinda happy.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: The intel I just shared about the ruins could fetch a high price. But since the children consider you family, it's only natural that I freely share it with you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Got it — so all we gotta do is go to some ruins, right? We can handle that!

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Excuse me, but may I tag along?

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: You wish to join, Miss Navia?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But... Are you sure you're up to exploring some ruins? You need to rest!

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Well, I'm sad, yes, but I can't just go back and plop myself into a chair by the roadside and do nothing.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: There's no point in being depressed while we still have a disaster on our hands. As my father's successor, I must live up to the hopes he had in me.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Besides, I'm also doing this for myself. I need something — a distraction — to keep my mind off Melus and Silver.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Navia's strong, but she needs company right now. We can be that company if she goes to explore the ruins with us.)

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: #Since you put it that way, I have no objections. What do you say, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We'll go to the ruins together.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Alright. The ruins are to the south of Poisson — here's the map.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, the three of us will handle it! C'mon, let's pack up and get going!

choices.text: Can you trust an outsider like me?

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: If you're concerned about things at the Palais, why don't you take some time to go up and check things out?

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: I believe you should still have some vacation time to spend.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Ah, thank you for being so understanding. It means a lot!

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: It's been some time since I've gone to the surface — I must say that I've started to miss it a little.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: The two of you have my thanks. If you need any help, just let me know.

dialogues.speaker: Disaster Victim (M)
dialogues.text: Oww! Don't move me, don't move me! I—I'm scared... Give me some space...
